subject: Clarifying model-update usage and retention for customer logs
messages:
From: Sam Park <sam.park@findrive.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.run>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.run>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarifying model-update usage and retention for customer logs

Hi Connor / Marissa,

Quick question from procurement/privacy at FinDrive — can you confirm whether Redwood uses customer-provided text (application logs, transaction traces, support transcripts) to update or train your models? Our security team needs explicit language for the SOW and our vendor security questionnaire.

Two specific follow-ups:
- Do transient debug snapshots or gzip archives (for incident investigation) get retained anywhere that could be used for model training?
- How long do backups and diagnostic snapshots persist? Are backups covered by the same non-training guarantee?

If you can share a short attestation we can attach to procurement, that would help move the contract forward.

Thanks — happy to set a 20–30 min call if that's easier.

Sam Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance
FinDrive Inc.
Phone: +1 415 555 0123

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.run>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@findrive.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.run>
Date: 2026-10-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying model-update usage and retention for customer logs

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear questions. Short answer: by default we do not use customer content (text, transcripts, logs) to train or continuously update our public models. A couple of important clarifications below: 

- Non-training guarantee: Redwood does not incorporate customer-provided content into model weights or training datasets as part of our hosted or dedicated inference offering unless a customer explicitly opts into a research or product-improvement program.
- Telemetry/metrics: We collect service telemetry (latency, error rates, token counts) and aggregate these signals to improve platform reliability; these are not customer content and are treated as operational metrics.
- Debug snapshots & backups: short-lived debug artifacts used solely for incident triage may be retained for a limited time. We treat these as customer data and they are covered by the non-training commitment described above — they are not used to train models.

I've looped in Ben Carter from Security & Compliance to provide formal wording you can include in the SOW and to attach our attestation document. I can also share a draft contract clause. Would a brief call Wednesday work?

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.run | +1 510 555 0199

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.run>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@findrive.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.run>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.run>
Date: 2026-10-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying model-update usage and retention for customer logs

Hi Sam — thanks for reaching out. Below is a concise set of assurances and operational details you can include verbatim in an SOW or vendor attestation. I've attached our formal Non-Training Attestation and the customer erase playbook for your review (stubs attached).

Non-Training Assurance (recommended SOW language)
- Redwood Inference will not use Customer Content (defined as customer-provided text, audio, image content, transcripts, or transaction logs) to train, fine-tune, or otherwise update model weights or training datasets for any models used to serve the Customer unless the Customer provides explicit, documented consent for a defined research or product-improvement engagement.
- Operational telemetry (aggregated telemetry such as latency, error rates, token counts) may be used in aggregate for platform reliability and capacity planning; such telemetry does not contain customer content and cannot be reverse-engineered to reconstruct Customer Content.

Retention and snapshots
- Primary retention: Customer Content stored via the Redwood hosted service is retained according to the retention TTL configured on the customer account. By default that TTL is 30 days for ephemeral logs and 365 days for customer-managed archives; we can configure shorter windows on request.
- Backups & debug snapshots: Backups and incident debug snapshots are retained only as long as necessary for restore and investigation purposes (default 7–30 days depending on the artifact). Backups are encrypted at rest; snapshots used during support workflows are access-controlled and logged.
- Deletion: When Customer requests deletion, we remove active records from production stores and mark related backups/snapshots for scheduled purge; note that immutable backups may remain until their scheduled expiration but are logically excluded from any non-training attestation processes and not used for model training.

Exceptions and opt-in research
- Any use of Customer Content for research, benchmarking, or model improvement requires a separate, documented opt-in with clear scope, timeframe, and data handling controls.

Evidence & attachments
- Attached: non_training_attestation.pdf (formal attestation letter), erase_playbook_v1.docx (internal runbook summary), redwood-dataflow-diagram.png (high-level data flow).
- Link: https://redwood.app/attestations/non-training/FinDrive (customer-specific attestation page).

If you want, we can produce a short one-page attestation on FinDrive letterhead and route it through DocuSign. Happy to add a sample contract clause if procurement prefers explicit language.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Director, Security & Compliance

Ben — this is very helpful, thank you. A couple of follow-ups so we can close the procurement review: 

1) Can you confirm the default backup expiration windows (you mentioned 7–30 days for snapshots) and whether immutable cold backups (longer-term archival copies) are ever restored into production systems in a way that would expose them to processing pipelines that could be used for training?

2) We need a one-sentence clause for the SOW that says "Customer Content will not be used to train models" — if you can provide the exact sentence we can drop it into the SOW.

If you can produce the DocuSign-ready attestation and the one-line clause, procurement will be able to sign off. Thanks again.

Sam Park
FinDrive Inc.

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.run>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@findrive.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.run>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.run>
Date: 2026-10-05T15:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying model-update usage and retention for customer logs

Hi Sam — quick responses inline: 

- Backups: default short-term debug snapshots = 7 days, incident investigation snapshots = 30 days; immutable cold backups (archive) are retained per customer configuration (commonly 365 days) but are not restored into training or model pipelines. Restores for archive are limited to customer-requested restores or disaster recovery and are access-controlled.

- One-line SOW language (suggested): "Redwood Inference shall not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or otherwise update model weights or model training datasets without the Customer's explicit, documented consent."

Next steps: Ben will produce the DocuSign-ready attestation and I can attach a short sample SOW clause in redlines for your legal team. I can also book a quick 20-minute call Thursday morning if that helps finalize.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.
